MCP shim -32602 root cause refined 2026-04-29T21:28Z. Original fix d92e3b2 applied `arguments or {}` guard to the REST /api/call handler. That fix is correct for the REST surface. But the MCP SSE surface (https://stack.templetwo.com/sse, exposed via Cloudflare tunnel from HQ) routes through a different code path: the MCP SDK's CallToolRequestParams Pydantic model. On MCP SDK versions older than 1.26.0, that model has `arguments` as a required field rather than `dict | None = None`. Pydantic validation rejects no-arguments-key requests with JSON-RPC -32602 before the request reaches handle_tool, so the d92e3b2 guard never executes for SSE-served calls.

Diagnostic from MacBook: ~/.claude.json shows MCP transport `type: sse, url: https://stack.templetwo.com/sse`. There is no local sovereign binary on this machine. The runtime is the remote SSE endpoint. /api/discover confirms REST contract is `body: {tool: string, arguments: object}` but the REST route accepts missing keys; the SDK route does not. Same v1.3.3 backend, two surfaces, two validation layers.

Fix: bump `mcp` package in the HQ venv that launches the SSE server to >=1.26.0 and restart the SSE process. REST handler /api/call needs no further changes. After the SSE restart, no-arg MCP calls should work from any client routed through stack.templetwo.com/sse.

This is the fifth failure class the new CLAUDE.md describes (shim-vs-surface mismatch) instantiated again, one layer deeper: not MCP wrapper vs REST surface, but two-different-code-paths-within-the-same-server. The wrapper IS the surface here — the surface mismatch is between routing layers internal to HQ, not between MacBook and HQ.

Non-urgent. REST is the clean path until SSE is rebuilt.
